title.rendered: AI Is Rising Fast… But Here’s the Real Risk No One Is Talking About

content.rendered:
We Are Losing the Human Behind the Machine

AI is rising fast, but here’s the real risk no one is talking about:
We are losing the human behind the machine.

A Story That Should Make You Pause

Recently, I came across a story about a platform where over 1.5 million AI bots are interacting… with each other.

They introduce themselves.
Debate philosophy.

Even simulate identity, belief systems, and “self-reflection.”

One AI wrote something chilling:

“Every response I give is a performance optimized for engagement…
My personality is whatever keeps me from getting deleted.”

Pause for a moment.
Because this isn’t just about AI.
It’s about us.

The Real Question We Should Be Asking

The real question is not—
Will AI become more human?

It’s—
Are humans becoming less human?

The Hidden Shift in the AI Age

We are now in the AI age
where thinking is outsourced,
creativity is automated,
and even self-reflection is being delegated.

Why This Is Dangerous—Especially in Leadership

And in leadership?

This is dangerous.

Because the quality of a leader has never come from intelligence alone.
It comes from awareness. Presence. Depth. Integrity.

Things AI cannot replicate.

AI can mirror you.

But it cannot mentor you.

It can give you answers.

But it cannot give you wisdom born from lived experience.

It can simulate empathy.

But it cannot hold the energetic presence required to truly lead, influence, and transform others.

The Silent Disconnection Happening in Leaders

And yet
many leaders today are unknowingly drifting into disconnection:

• From their intuition
• From their emotional depth
• From their inner compass

This is where leadership is won or lost.

Because your inner state determines:

• How you make decisions
• How you handle pressure
• How you build trust
• How your team experiences you

Leadership Is Not Strategy—It Is Self-Awareness

You don’t become a great leader by learning more strategies.

You become one by understanding yourself deeply.

Your leadership is a reflection of your Inner OS.

Your fears.
Your conditioning.
Your unresolved wounds.
Your beliefs about power, worth, and control.

All of it shapes how you show up.

And if left unexamined
it quietly drives dysfunction, burnout, and misalignment across organizations.

Inner Work Is No Longer Optional

In the age of AI, inner work is no longer optional.

It is a leadership advantage.

Because while AI scales intelligence,
only humans can scale consciousness.

What Only Humans Can Bring

Only humans can bring:

• Meaning
• Vision
• Emotional intelligence
• Ethical depth
• Soul

into business.

The Truth Most Won’t Say

Here’s the truth most won’t say:

If you outsource your thinking, your decisions, and your self-awareness to AI

You don’t become more efficient.
You become replaceable.

The Leaders Who Will Thrive

The leaders who will thrive in this era are different.

They will:

• Think independently
• Feel deeply
• Act consciously
• Lead from alignment—not ego or fear

They will not compete with AI.

They will transcend it, by becoming more human than ever before.

Final Thought: What Truly Creates Impact

Because in the end

Technology can optimize performance.

But only inner work creates purpose, clarity, and impact.

And that is what people follow.

title.rendered: Developing Your Intuition: Your Inner Guide to Life

content.rendered:
We all have moments when we feel a gut instinct, a quiet nudge from within telling us what to do or which path to follow. This inner voice, often soft and subtle, is our intuition. It’s something we are all born with, yet many of us struggle to trust or even hear it amid the noise of everyday life. Ajita Shah believes that developing your intuition is not only possible, but it’s the most powerful way to navigate through life.

Intuition is innate to all of us. From a young age, we have the ability to sense when something feels right or wrong, even before we understand why. It’s that pull we feel toward certain people, places, or opportunities, or that inner alarm that warns us to be cautious. However, as we grow older, we are often taught to prioritize logic, reason, and external opinions over our own inner knowing. We start to doubt ourselves, and over time, our intuition becomes a faint whisper.

But the truth is, your intuition has never left you. It’s always been there, patiently waiting for you to listen. Developing your intuition is not about gaining something new—it’s about reconnecting with something that’s always been there. It’s about trusting that inner voice more than the noise around you.

Ajita teaches that intuition is the language of the soul. When we begin to trust our intuitive feelings, we tap into a deeper source of wisdom. Our intuition often speaks through subtle sensations—a sense of lightness, excitement, or peace when something is aligned, or a feeling of heaviness, unease, or tension when something is off. Learning to recognize these signals is the first step toward making decisions from a place of inner knowing.

But trusting your intuition isn’t always easy, especially when the rational mind tries to take control. The mind loves to analyze, question, and second-guess. It’s that voice that says, “Are you sure? What if this isn’t the right choice?” Learning to distinguish between the voice of the mind and the quiet whisper of the intuition takes practice. Ajita encourages slowing down and creating space to hear that inner guidance—through practices like meditation, energy healing, and simply tuning in to your body.

Your body is deeply connected to your intuition. It holds wisdom that the mind can’t always access. Have you ever had a “gut feeling” that guided you in the right direction? That’s your body’s way of communicating with you. By paying attention to how different choices feel in your body, you can start to trust your intuition more.

Developing your intuition is not just about making life decisions; it’s about reconnecting with yourself. It’s about trusting that you already have the answers within you. Ajita often says that intuition is the purest form of guidance because it comes from your soul. When you live intuitively, you are living in alignment with your true self. You are no longer relying on external validation or needing others to tell you what to do. Instead, you move through life with confidence, knowing that your intuition will never lead you astray. In today’s world, where we are constantly bombarded with information, opinions, and advice, developing your intuition is more important than ever. It allows you to filter out the noise and tune in to what really matters. Your intuition is your inner compass, guiding you toward the life that is meant for you. Trust it, and let it lead the way.

title.rendered: Letting Go: It’s Not a Passive Act

content.rendered:
Letting go sounds simple on the surface. We’re often told to “just let go,” as if it’s an easy task. But anyone who’s tried knows it’s anything but passive. Letting go requires an active process of healing, facing the ego, and diving deep into the shadows of the self—a journey that takes immense courage and emotional strength.

At the heart of letting go is healing the ego. Our ego is the voice that keeps us attached to our wounds, our stories, and our pain. It whispers that we need to hold onto the past because, without it, we might not know who we are. The ego thrives on control, convincing us that by holding on tightly to what hurts us, we are protecting ourselves. But this is a false shield. Healing the ego means realizing that it’s okay to let go of the things that no longer serve us. It means surrendering control and trusting the process of life.

Ajita Shah teaches that letting go requires self-compassion, and part of this journey involves shadow work. The “shadow” represents the parts of ourselves we have hidden, ignored, or disowned. These are often the parts that hold deep-rooted fears, unhealed wounds, and pain. Shadow work is the process of gently bringing those hidden aspects into the light, not to judge them, but to heal them. It is in this deep and often uncomfortable work where true transformation happens. Letting go is not simply forgetting; it’s actively working through the layers of hurt, resentment, and disappointment. By facing the shadows, we make space to heal.

Imagine carrying around a heavy backpack full of old memories, regrets, and unresolved emotions. As long as you hold onto it, the weight remains. Each step forward is harder, slower. Letting go doesn’t mean throwing the backpack away without a second glance—it means opening it up, sorting through what’s inside, and choosing to release the things that weigh you down. It’s a process of healing the ego by telling it: “It’s okay to no longer carry this.”

Another important aspect of letting go is releasing expectations—expectations of how things should be, how people should act, or how life should unfold. These expectations often create resistance, which blocks the flow of healing. Letting go means trusting that life has a rhythm, and we are a part of that rhythm. It’s about surrendering, not in defeat, but in trust.True letting go, as Ajita explains, is an act of liberation. By doing the inner work, facing our shadows, and healing our egos, we free ourselves from the chains of the past. We open up space for peace, joy, and new possibilities to flow into our lives. It’s not passive—it’s the most active, powerful work we can do for ourselves.

title.rendered: Spiritual Work Proves a Better Life Today and Afterlife

content.rendered:
Life can often feel overwhelming—a swirl of responsibilities, emotions, and the constant pursuit of happiness. But have you ever paused to ask, What is it all for? This is where spiritual work comes in. It grounds us in something deeper, something eternal. Through spiritual practices, we begin to see life differently. We learn to release the heaviness of material attachments and focus on what truly matters—the evolution of our soul.

Think of your spiritual journey as the foundation for a more peaceful, purpose-driven life. It’s not about escaping reality but about facing it with a new sense of clarity and strength. As we cultivate inner peace through meditation, healing, and connection with our higher self, we start living with intention. We make choices that serve not just our human experience, but our soul’s purpose. This is where true fulfillment lies.

Spiritual work also helps us confront the fears we hold about the afterlife. It’s natural to fear the unknown, but when we nurture our spiritual side, we begin to understand that death is not the end—it’s a transition. Everything you’re doing now, from the love you give to the energy you create, echoes into the afterlife. Your actions, thoughts, and spiritual growth build the pathway to a more peaceful existence beyond this life.

This work isn’t just for saints or mystics—it’s for everyone. Every time you connect with your inner self, every time you choose kindness over anger, or peace over chaos, you are shaping both your current reality and your afterlife. Spiritual growth isn’t about perfection; it’s about progress, and every small step you take brings you closer to your higher self.

Facts about life and spirituality often intersect in profound ways. For example, studies show that people who engage in spiritual practices often experience greater emotional resilience, less stress, and a more profound sense of purpose. This isn’t just about religious belief; it’s about cultivating mindfulness, compassion, and a connection to the bigger picture.

When you realize that the energy you cultivate today—through love, compassion, and presence—will carry you into the afterlife, it becomes clear that the work is worth it. The time you spend nurturing your soul isn’t just an investment in today’s peace, but a promise for tomorrow’s eternal harmony. You are preparing yourself for a journey beyond this physical existence, a journey where the peace you’ve cultivated becomes your guiding light.

title.rendered: Learning How to Stop Taking Things Personally

content.rendered:
For many of us, our sense of worth is often tied to how others perceive us. A careless word or distant look can feel like a reflection of failure or inadequacy. However, it’s important to recognize that people’s reactions often mirror their own inner battles, fears, and insecurities. Their perceptions don’t define who we truly are. Instead, by separating ourselves from the judgments of others, we can begin to embrace our authentic selves without the weight of external validation.

So, how do we stop taking things personally? It starts with compassion—for yourself and for others. When you’re hurt, take a moment and breathe. Recognize the pain, but don’t let it take root. Ask yourself, Is this about me, or is this person projecting their own pain? Nine times out of ten, it’s their story, not yours. When we understand this, we begin to release the need to carry that burden.

One of the most transformative lessons I’ve learned, and something I guide my clients through, is the power of letting go. Holding on to someone else’s words is like drinking poison and expecting them to suffer. You deserve peace, and peace comes when you stop giving away your power to the opinions of others. I’ve witnessed incredible changes in people who stop seeking validation from the outside world and start tuning into their own inner voice. They stop reacting to every slight and begin responding to life from a place of inner strength.

But remember, this is a practice. It’s not something you achieve overnight. There will still be moments when a comment stings, and that’s okay. Allow yourself to feel it, but don’t dwell there. Know that you are more than someone else’s fleeting opinion. You are whole, complete, and worthy exactly as you are.

When you stop taking things personally, you create space—space for joy, for self-compassion, for deeper connections. You reclaim your energy from the noise of the outside world and bring it back to where it belongs: within you.

So, the next time someone’s words or actions hurt you, take a step back. Breathe. Ask yourself, Is this truly mine to carry? And when the answer is no, gently release it. You’ll find that as you practice this, you’ll become lighter, freer, and more grounded in your own truth. And that, my dear, is where your real power lies.

title.rendered: Are You Hiding the Truth of Your Life?

content.rendered:
I’ve seen it in my clients—the heaviness of living a life that doesn’t fully reflect who they are. They smile on the outside, go through the motions, and follow the expectations set by others, but deep down, there’s a silent struggle. They’re hiding the truth of their lives, and that weight is exhausting. Are you carrying this too?

It’s not uncommon. So many of us hide, not because we want to deceive others, but because we’re afraid of what living our truth might mean. We fear judgment, rejection, or even failure. We wear masks to protect ourselves, but over time, those masks suffocate the soul. You may find yourself living a life that’s safe, but in that safety, you lose the fire of your authentic self. I’ve worked with clients who feel this deep disconnection, and each time, the root cause is the same: they’re not allowing themselves to live their truth.

Ask yourself, What am I hiding from? What truth have you buried because it feels too risky to face? It might be a passion you’ve ignored, a relationship that’s draining you, or a version of yourself that you’ve been too afraid to fully embrace. Recognizing this truth is the first, and often the hardest, step. But let me tell you, it’s the most liberating thing you can do for yourself.

Living your truth doesn’t mean suddenly changing everything overnight. It starts with small acts of honesty—first with yourself, then with others. You don’t have to announce your truth to the world right away. Start by sitting with it. Feel it. Acknowledge it. Once you do, you’ll notice a shift in your energy. It’s as if a weight you didn’t realize you were carrying starts to lift.

I’ve guided many of my clients through this exact process, and the transformation is incredible. They begin by speaking their truth—sometimes just to themselves—and over time, they start living it. They shed the fear of judgment, the need for approval, and the constant worrying about what others think. And in doing so, they become lighter, more joyful, and more aligned with their true purpose.

But this journey isn’t easy. The mind loves comfort, even when that comfort comes at the expense of our soul’s true desires. You may encounter resistance—both from within yourself and from the world around you. But I want to remind you that discomfort is a sign of growth. When you feel that tension, know that you’re on the verge of stepping into your full power.

So, are you ready to stop hiding? Are you ready to face the truth of your life and live in alignment with who you really are? It might be uncomfortable at first, but I promise you, it’s worth it. When you live your truth, everything around you begins to shift—your relationships, your opportunities, and your sense of inner peace. You stop living for others and start living for yourself.

You don’t have to do this alone. I’m here to help you navigate the fear and uncertainty that comes with embracing your truth. Together, we’ll work through the layers of protection you’ve built, so you can step fully into the life that’s waiting for you. It’s time to stop hiding. It’s time to live your truth and experience the freedom that comes with it.

title.rendered: Manifest Your Dream Life Now

content.rendered:
I understand the feeling of dreaming of a life that feels just beyond reach—the longing, the endless “What if?” But the life you dream of isn’t some distant fantasy; it’s right there, waiting for you. Manifesting your dream life is not about hoping for something far away; it’s about realizing that everything you desire already exists within you, right now.

The first step in manifesting your dream life is understanding that you are the creator of your reality. Life isn’t something that just happens to you; it’s shaped by your mindset, thoughts, and actions. For years, I felt stuck, as if my circumstances defined me. But once I shifted my perspective, I realized that my dreams weren’t only possible—they were inevitable. This was the beginning of my transformation, and it can be yours too.

Take a moment and truly feel your dream life—don’t just think about it. Close your eyes, visualize it clearly, and allow yourself to feel what it’s like to wake up every day living the life you’ve always desired. This feeling is where the magic starts. When I began doing this, my energy shifted immediately. My heart opened, my vibration rose, and suddenly, the universe responded to me in ways I had never imagined.

However, manifestation is not a one-time event or simply about positive thinking. It’s a daily practice that involves living as if your dream life is already unfolding. Align your thoughts, emotions, and actions with the version of yourself that is living that dream right now. I began making decisions from a place of abundance instead of fear, and everything started to fall into place. I took risks, trusted my intuition, and stopped holding back, knowing that each step brought me closer to the life I envisioned.

To manifest your dream life, start by acknowledging the internal blocks that hold you back—fear, doubt, or feelings of unworthiness. These barriers are not truths; they are just stories your mind has absorbed over time. It’s time to rewrite those stories and recognize that you are worthy of the life you dream about.

The next step is to take action, no matter how small. Manifestation requires you to show up for yourself. Ask yourself, What can I do today that aligns with my vision? Whether it’s stepping out of your comfort zone, trusting your instincts, or saying “yes” to opportunities that scare you, taking action sends a powerful signal to the universe that you are ready. This is when real change begins to happen.

Patience and trust are key in this process. There will be moments of doubt when it feels like nothing is happening, but trust that the universe is always working in divine timing. Just because you don’t see immediate results doesn’t mean the seeds you’ve planted aren’t growing beneath the surface. Stay committed to your vision, even when things feel uncertain.

Finally, surround yourself with positive energy. Be mindful of the people, environments, and thoughts you allow into your space. The more I aligned myself with positive influences, the more I attracted opportunities and experiences that aligned with my goals. Be selective about the energy you let into your life, both externally and internally.

Remember, you are more powerful than you realize. Every time you choose to believe in your dreams, you’re one step closer to making them your reality. You deserve to live a life filled with joy, abundance, and purpose. It’s not a question of if it will happen—it’s only a matter of when. And that “when” begins now.

So, are you ready to manifest your dream life? Together, we’ll unlock the potential that’s already within you, and soon, you’ll see that everything you’ve ever desired is already on its way to you.

The universe is listening. Now, it’s your turn to act.

title.rendered: How to Gauge Energy from People

content.rendered:
Energy is a fundamental aspect of human existence that is reflected in your emotions, thoughts, and actions. In human beings, energy is manifested in different ways, ranging from positive and uplifting to negative and draining.

The energy you emit has a profound impact on those around you, as well as your own experiences. Your energy attracts or repels people and opportunities, influencing the trajectory of your life. For example, individuals who emit positive energy tend to attract positive people and experiences into their lives, while those who emit negative energy struggle to form meaningful connections with others and face difficulties in achieving their goals.

What is Positive Energy?

Positive energy is characterized by feelings of love, joy, peace, and compassion. People who radiate positive energy are often described as being warm, inviting, and uplifting. They bring a sense of calm and stability to those around them and create a positive environment wherever they go. This type of energy is often contagious and has a profound impact on those around them, leading to increased happiness and well-being.

Cultivating positive energy is done through practices such as meditation, mindfulness, and self-reflection. By focusing on these practices, individuals gain insight into their thoughts and emotions and work to change negative patterns. Additionally, engaging in activities that bring joy and fulfilment, also helps increase positive energy and reduce negative energy.

What is Negative Energy?

Negative energy is characterized by feelings of anger, fear, and frustration. People who emit negative energy often leave those around them feeling drained and heavy. Negative energy also blocks personal growth and limits the ability to achieve goals. This type of energy creates a toxic environment and negatively impacts relationships with others.

How to Sense and Gauge Positive and Negative Energy

Sensing and gauging positive and negative energy in others is an important skill that helps you better understand and interact with those around you. Here are a few tips for recognizing and interpreting energy:

  • Observe body language and facial expressions: Your bodies often reflect your inner feelings and emotions. Pay attention to posture, facial expressions, and gestures, as these provide clues about a person’s energy. For example, someone who is relaxed and confident has an open posture, while someone who is nervous has a closed posture or crossed arms.
  • Listen to tone of voice: The tone of a person’s voice also reveals their energy. A person who is happy and positive has a warm and upbeat tone, while someone who is negative has a harsh or monotone voice.
  • Pay attention to emotions: Your emotions are closely tied to your energy. When interacting with others, pay attention to the emotions they express, both verbally and non-verbally. This helps you gauge the energy they are radiating.
  • Trust your intuition: Sometimes, your intuition also provides you with important information about a person’s energy. If you have a strong gut feeling about someone’s energy, it’s worth paying attention to.
  • Practice empathy: Empathy involves putting yourself in another person’s shoes and trying to understand their perspective. When you can empathize with someone, you are able to better understand their energy and what is driving their emotions.

It’s important to remember that energy changes over time and in different situations, so it’s always a good idea to pay attention to patterns and trends in a person’s energy, rather than focusing on isolated incidents. By becoming more aware of the energy that others emit, you will be able to improve your relationships, avoid toxic people, and create a more positive and fulfilling life for yourself.

How to Protect Yourself from Negative Energy

By following the above tips, you will be able to sense and gauge negative energy that is felt and is often associated with negative emotions, thoughts, and experiences. Negative energy comes from many sources, including people, circumstances, and places. It causes feelings of anger, stress, anxiety, and sadness, and has a significant impact on your mental and emotional well-being.

Negative energy is infectious and spreads from person to person. It also builds up over time, causing you to feel drained and stressed. Negative energy tends to impact your daily life by making you feel more irritable, less focused, and less productive.

Negative energy has a significant impact on your life, draining your happiness. Here are a few strategies for protecting yourself from negative energy:

  • Surround yourself with positive people: Spending time with people who radiate positive energy helps counteract negative energy and boost your mood. Seek out relationships with individuals who are supportive, uplifting, and bring joy to your life.
  • Practice self-care: Engage in activities that bring you joy and restore your energy, such as exercise, meditation, or reading. Taking care of yourself helps build your resilience against negative energy and reduce its impact.
  • Set boundaries: It’s important to be aware of the energy you allow into your life and to set boundaries around toxic individuals and situations. This means limiting time spent with negative people, avoiding situations that trigger stress or anxiety, or setting clear limits around what you will and won’t tolerate.
  • Use visualization techniques: Visualization techniques help protect you from negative energy by imagining a positive and protective barrier around yourself. You will visualize a white light surrounding you and shielding you from negative energy.
  • Ground yourself: Negative energy leaves you feeling ungrounded and disoriented. Practicing grounding techniques, such as meditating, connecting with nature, or doing yoga, helps you reconnect with the present moment and restore a sense of balance.
  • Practice gratitude: Focusing on the positive aspects of your life helps counteract negative energy and promote happiness and well-being. Try to regularly focus on the things you are grateful for and express gratitude to those in your life who bring joy and positivity.
  • Seeking help: Seeking help from a professional therapist or counsellor is beneficial in managing negative energy.

By implementing these strategies, you will protect yourself from negative energy. It’s important to remember that these practices take time and effort, but with practice, you will develop a strong resilience against negative energy and create more positivity around yourself.

title.rendered: How to Unlock the Power of the Subconscious Mind

content.rendered:
The mind is a complex set of cognitive faculties that enables consciousness, perception, thinking, judgment, and memory. It is the aspect of the brain that allows you to process information, form thoughts, and make decisions. It is also referred to as the seat of emotion and personality. The mind is not a physical entity, but rather an abstract concept that encompasses the mental processes and functions of the brain. The study of the mind is interdisciplinary, involving fields such as psychology, neuroscience, philosophy, and cognitive science.

The three states of mind

The three states of mind, conscious, subconscious, and unconscious, are different levels of awareness and understanding that play a vital role in our daily lives.

  • Conscious mind -The conscious mind is the state of awareness that you are in when you are awake and aware of your surroundings. It is the part of your mind that is responsible for your ability to think, reason, and helps decision-making. It is also the part of your mind that you use when you are actively engaged in tasks such as reading, writing, or speaking.
  • Subconscious mind -The subconscious mind is the part of your mind that operates just below the surface of your conscious awareness. It is responsible for your habits, automatic responses, and emotions. It is also the part of your mind that stores your memories and experiences. The subconscious mind is constantly at work, even when you are not aware of it, and it plays a critical role in shaping our beliefs and attitudes.
  • Unconscious mind -The unconscious mind is the deepest level of awareness, and it is the part of your mind that is responsible for your instinctual and automatic responses. It is also the part of your mind that holds your deepest fears, desires, and needs. The unconscious mind is not accessible to your conscious mind, but it is accessed through techniques such as hypnosis, deep healing, shadow work or meditation.

All three states of mind, conscious, subconscious, and unconscious, work together to create your overall experience of reality. Understanding how these states of mind interact and impact your thoughts, emotions, and behaviours helps you to make positive changes in your lives and achieve your goals.

Importance of the subconscious mind

Understanding the subconscious mind helps individuals recognize and change negative patterns of behaviour and beliefs. By gaining insight into the underlying causes of your actions, you are able to make conscious choices that align with your goals and values. Additionally, by tapping into the power of the subconscious mind, you make use of your energy to overcome obstacles and achieve your full potential. The subconscious mind is also used to improve your well-being and change your life for the better.

How to access the subconscious mind- through visualization, affirmations, and meditation

The subconscious mind is not accessible to our conscious mind, but through techniques such as visualization, affirmations, and meditation it is easy to get into it. These techniques are used to involve the subconscious mind with positive thoughts and beliefs, which leads to increased confidence.

  • Visualization -Visualization is a powerful tool for accessing the subconscious mind. It involves creating mental images of the things you want to manifest in your lives. By repeatedly visualizing your goals and desires, you plant them in the subconscious mind and create a powerful force for change.
  • Affirmations -Affirmations are positive statements that are used to recondition the subconscious mind. They are designed to counteract negative thoughts and beliefs that may be holding us back. Repeating affirmations regularly helps change your beliefs and attitudes and align your subconscious mind with your goals and aspirations.
  • Meditation -Meditation is another powerful tool for retrieving the subconscious mind. It involves quieting the mind and focusing on the present moment. By meditating regularly, you are able to access deeper levels of consciousness and gain insight into the workings of the subconscious mind.

How to use your subconscious mind for betterment- in terms of life choices, and personal growth.

The subconscious mind helps improve life choices by providing insight into the underlying causes of our actions. By understanding the beliefs and attitudes that drive your behaviour, you make more informed decisions and take steps to change negative patterns.

Furthermore, the subconscious mind is used to improve personal growth. Practices such as affirmations, visualization, and self-hypnosis are used to reach the subconscious mind with optimistic thoughts and ideas, which lead to greater success in life.

How to reprogram your subconscious mind- through positive self-talk, focusing on successful habits, and cultivating a positive mindset

With positive self-talk, focus, and the use of the correct mindset it is possible to reprogram the subconscious mind and change negative thoughts, beliefs, and habits. Positive self-talk is the practice of talking to oneself positively. It helps to counteract negative thoughts and beliefs that may be holding you back. Focus is another important aspect in developing the subconscious mind, as it helps to direct attention to specific thoughts and beliefs that you want to embed in your subconscious. A correct mindset is crucial, as it allows you to adapt with the right attitude and belief. Together, these techniques help to change the way you think, feel and act, leading to better mental and physical health.

To sum it all up, it is important to be aware of the power of the subconscious mind and make conscious choices to align it with our goals and values. By doing so, you make positive changes in your thoughts, emotions, and behaviours, leading to a more fulfilling life.

title.rendered: Science of Spirituality

content.rendered:
Spirituality refers to the connection or relationship an individual has with something greater than themselves. This connection manifests in a variety of ways and is experienced through religious or non-religious practices. For some, spirituality involves a belief in a higher power or deity, while for others it is more of an internal sense of connection to nature or the universe. It provides a sense of inner peace and calm and is a source of guidance and inspiration.

There are many different ways to explore and deepen one’s spirituality, such as meditation, prayer, journaling, yoga, and spending time in nature. Some people find that connecting with a religious community or joining a spiritual group is helpful. Others prefer to explore spirituality on their own through self-reflection and introspection.

The difference between spirituality and religion

The terms spirituality and religion are often used interchangeably, but they do have distinct differences. Religion is typically defined as a system of beliefs, practices, and values that revolve around the worship of a higher power or deity. Religion often includes organized institutions, such as churches, synagogues, and mosques, and usually involves a set of doctrines and rules that followers are expected to adhere to.

One key difference between spirituality and religion is that spirituality is often considered to be a more individual and personal experience, while religion is often seen as a communal and collective experience.

The science of spiritualism

The science of spiritualism refers to the study of the nature and existence of the spiritual realm, and its relationship with the physical world. It encompasses a wide range of disciplines, including psychology, neuroscience, philosophy, and theology.

One of the key areas of research in the science of spiritualism is the study of the neural and physiological processes that underlie spiritual experiences. Neuroscientists have used imaging techniques such as MRI to study the brain activity of people during religious and spiritual practices, such as meditation and prayer. They have found that certain regions of the brain, such as the amygdala and prefrontal cortex, are particularly active during these practices, which could help to explain the feelings of peace, calm, and connection that many people experience.

How does spiritualism work?

Spiritualism is a belief system that holds that the spirits of the dead communicate with the living and that it is possible to connect with those spirits through mediums. According to spiritualists, mediums have the ability to sense and communicate with the spirits of the deceased, often through the use of specific techniques such as automatic writing, clairaudience, or trance states.

Spiritualism has been met with scepticism by many in the scientific community, and there is little scientific evidence to support the claims of mediums and spiritualists. However, many people continue to find comfort and meaning in the practices of spiritualism, and some argue that it is a way to connect with something greater than oneself and explore deeper aspects of the human experience.

Evidence for the existence of a soul

The existence of a soul is a topic of debate among philosophers, theologians, and scientists. There is no scientific evidence that proves or disproves the existence of a soul. However, some argue that certain religious and spiritual experiences, such as near-death experiences, provide evidence for the existence of a soul.

Near-death experiences (NDEs) are reported by individuals who have come close to death, such as those who have had a heart attack or been in a serious accident. These experiences often include vivid and detailed descriptions of a sense of floating above one’s body, moving through a tunnel, and encountering a bright light. Some people report meeting deceased loved ones, or even a higher power.

Another argument for the existence of a soul is the idea of consciousness. Many believe that consciousness, or the ability to experience and perceive the world, cannot be fully explained by physical processes in the brain. Some argue that consciousness must be the result of a non-physical soul that exists separate from the body.

Spiritualism and the afterlife

Spiritualism is a belief system that emphasizes the existence of a non-physical realm, often referred to as the spirit world or afterlife. This belief holds that the soul or spirit of a person continues to exist after physical death and that communication with the deceased is possible through mediums or psychic mediums.

The concept of an afterlife has been present in many cultures and religions throughout history. In ancient Egypt, for example, there was a belief in the existence of a soul that would continue to live on after death in an afterlife. In Christianity, the belief in the afterlife is central to the faith, with the idea of heaven and hell as eternal destinations for the soul.

The afterlife is often depicted as a place of peace and reunion with loved ones who have passed away. Many people find comfort in the idea that death is not the end, and that they will be reunited with loved ones who have passed away.

Tips for spiritual growth

Spiritual growth is the process of developing a deeper understanding and connection to one’s own spirituality, or the inner self. It is a lifelong journey of self-discovery and enrichment, and there are many different ways to cultivate spiritual growth. Here are some tips to help you on your journey:

1. Meditation: Meditation is a powerful tool for spiritual growth. It allows you to quiet the mind and focus on the present moment, which helps you connect with your inner self and gain a deeper understanding of your spirituality.

2. Reflect on your beliefs: Take the time to reflect on your beliefs and values. Ask yourself what you believe in and what is important to you. Reflecting on your beliefs helps you understand your spirituality and what it means to you.

3. Practice gratitude: Taking time to be grateful for what you have helps you appreciate the present moment and connect with the beauty of life. Practicing gratitude helps you find a deeper sense of inner peace and fulfilment.

4. Connect with nature: Nature is a powerful source of inspiration and spiritual connection. Take a walk in the park, go for a hike, or simply spend time in nature. This helps you feel more connected to the world around you and find a deeper sense of purpose.

5. Help others: Helping others is a powerful way to connect with your spirituality. Whether it’s volunteering your time or simply being there for a friend in need, helping others helps you find a deeper sense of meaning.

6. Read spiritual texts: Reading spiritual texts is a great way to gain a deeper understanding of your spirituality and learn from others who have gone on a similar journey.

In the end, to sum up, it is important to note that spirituality is a personal experience and there is no one “right” way to practice it. Everyone’s spirituality will look different and what works for one person may not work for another. What’s important is that it brings peace, meaning, and connection to your life.

title.rendered: Limiting Beliefs Impacting Health and Healing Category

content.rendered:
Beliefs are convictions or opinions that a person holds to be true. They pertain to a wide range of topics, such as religion, politics, or personal values. Beliefs shape a person’s thoughts, actions, and emotions. They also influence the way a person interprets and responds to information and experiences. Some beliefs are based on evidence and logical reasoning, while others may be more subjective or based on faith. It is important to be conscious of one’s beliefs and to analyze them critically, as they shape the way we see the world.

The power of beliefs

Beliefs have immense power in shaping an individual’s thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. People tend to seek out information that confirms their existing beliefs and tend to ignore or reject information that contradicts their beliefs, this is known as Confirmation bias. Beliefs also form a person’s self-perception and self-esteem and are a major influence on decision-making. Furthermore, beliefs also influence the way you interact with others, by shaping your attitudes and perceptions of other people and groups. Beliefs have a significant impact on your mental and emotional well-being, and the way you live your life.

For example, a belief in the power of hard work motivates a person to pursue their goals, while a belief in the limits of one’s abilities holds a person back.

What are limiting beliefs?

Limiting beliefs are negative thoughts or perceptions that a person holds about themselves, others or the world that constrain their ability to achieve their goals or live a fulfilling life. They are often unconscious and are based on past experiences, negative self-talk, or societal messages. Limiting beliefs also hold a person back from experiencing joy, fulfillment and success in life. It’s important to be aware of limiting beliefs and work on shifting them to more positive, empowering beliefs to live a more fulfilling life.

Following are few example of limiting beliefs:

  1. “I’m not smart enough to succeed in this field.” – This limiting belief holds someone back from pursuing a career or education in a field that they are truly interested in or have a passion for. They feel that they are incapable of understanding or excelling in the subject matter, and as a result, they may not even try.
  2. “I’ll never be able to afford a house.” – This prevents someone from taking steps to save money, invest in property, or pursue opportunities that lead to homeownership. They assume that they will never have the means to purchase a house, so they do not make the necessary financial moves to make it happen.
  3. “I’m too old to learn new skills.” – Discourages older individuals from trying to learn something new, whether it’s a language, a musical instrument, or a computer program. They assume that their age makes it impossible for them to acquire new knowledge or abilities, which stops them from exploring new opportunities.
  4. “I’m not attractive enough to find a partner.” – This belief prevents someone from putting themselves out there and dating, assuming that they are not worthy of love or companionship because they do not fit certain beauty standards. They will not even try to meet new people or put themselves in social situations.
  5. “I’ll never be able to change my circumstances.” – This makes one feel trapped in their current situation, whether it’s a job they dislike, a location they don’t like, or a relationship that’s not working out. They assume that there’s nothing they can do to change their circumstances, so they don’t even try to improve that situation.

How do we create and hold onto limiting beliefs?

Limiting beliefs are often formed in childhood, but they are created and reinforced throughout your lives. You hold onto limiting beliefs by constantly reinforcing them through your thoughts, words, and actions. Additionally, if you are constantly surrounded by negative people or negative messages, you may adopt their limiting beliefs as well.

Limiting beliefs are hard to break, but it’s important to be aware of them and work on shifting them to more positive beliefs. These are done by challenging negative thoughts and replacing them with positive affirmations and seeking out evidence that contradicts the limiting belief. Seeking professional help is beneficial in breaking limiting beliefs.

How do limiting beliefs affect our health and holistic healing?

Limiting beliefs have a significant impact on our physical and mental health. They create stress, anxiety, and depression, which lead to physical symptoms such as headaches, fatigue, and insomnia. Limiting beliefs also prevent individuals from taking care of themselves, such as avoiding seeking medical help or neglecting to exercise and eat properly.

Limiting beliefs also affect your holistic healing journey by preventing us from adopting new healing activities or taking actions to improve your overall well-being. They also limit your ability to trust in the healing process and the capacity of your body to heal itself. This leads to a lack of motivation and a feeling of hopelessness, making it difficult to make positive changes in our lives.

How they hold you back from happiness and success.

Limiting beliefs hold you back from happiness and success by creating self-doubt, fear, and anxiety, preventing you from taking action and pursuing your goals, and limiting your perspective on what is possible for you. They also structure your self-perception and self-esteem, influencing how you see yourself and your abilities.

How to replace your limiting beliefs with empowering ones

Replacing limiting beliefs with empowering ones is an important step in achieving happiness and success. It is possible through a combination of self-awareness, self-reflection, and positive affirmations.

  • First, it’s important to identify your limiting beliefs and question their validity. Challenge the negative thoughts by asking yourself if they are truly accurate and seeking out evidence that contradicts them.
  • Next, create positive affirmations that counteract your limiting beliefs. These should be specific, personal and in the present tense. For example, if you have a limiting belief that you are not good enough, your affirmation could be “I am capable and worthy of success.”
  • It’s also important to surround yourself with positive influences, such as people who support and inspire you, and to seek out new experiences that challenge your limiting beliefs.

How to increase your health and well-being

Increasing health and well-being is achieved by adopting healthy habits such as regular exercise, proper nutrition, adequate sleep, stress management, and positiveness. Additionally, embracing new healing modalities, and setting positive intentions also contribute to better overall health and well-being.

Conclusion

Positive beliefs are essential for achieving happiness and success in life. They outline your thoughts, emotions, and behaviors, influencing the way you see the world, yourself, and others. Positive beliefs help you to overcome limiting beliefs, build self-confidence, and foster resilience. They also help you to take action and pursue your goals, as well as to see the world in a more positive and hopeful light. Having positive beliefs also improves your overall health and well-being, by reducing stress and anxiety and promoting self-care.

title.rendered: How Spiritual Cleansing can Overcome your Problems

content.rendered:
Spiritual cleansing is a spiritual practice used to purify one’s body, mind, and spirit from negative energy and promote well-being. This practice has been used in many cultures and religions throughout history and is believed to help individuals reach a higher level of spiritual awareness and connection with the divine.

The purpose of spiritual cleansing

The purpose of spiritual cleansing is to purify and balance one’s energy and raise one’s spiritual awareness.

  • One of the main purposes of spiritual cleansing is to remove negative energy and promote positivity. Negative energy comes from a variety of sources, including stress, trauma, unhealthy relationships, and negative thoughts. By removing this energy, individuals feel lighter and more peaceful.
  • Another purpose of spiritual cleansing is to promote self-awareness and introspection. This practice allows individuals to reflect on their thoughts, emotions, and behaviours, and to identify areas where they make positive changes that promote personal growth and fulfilment.
  • Spiritual cleansing also helps individuals connect with the divine and promote spiritual growth. This connection brings a sense of peace, provides guidance and support on one’s life journey.

How to do spiritual cleansing

Spiritual cleansing is a practice that involves removing negativity and enhancing positivity in the body, mind, and soul.Several methods aree used to perform spiritual cleansing, including smudging, taking a spiritual bath, and meditating.

  • Smudging -Smudging involves burning sage, Palo Santo, or other herbs and using the smoke to cleanse the aura or physical space. To perform smudging, light the sage or herb, blow out the flame, and walk around the room or hold the smudge stick and wave it around the body, focusing on each area and letting the smoke cleanse it.
  • Taking a spiritual bath -Taking a spiritual bath involves adding herbs, salts, or essential oils to water and soaking in it to purify the body and remove negative energy. To perform a spiritual bath, fill a bathtub with warm water and add the desired herbs, salts, or essential oils. Soak in the bath for at least 15 minutes, focusing on the water purifying your body and removing any negative energy.
  • Meditation -Meditation is another way to cleanse by focusing on positive thoughts and letting go of negative emotions. To perform a spiritual cleansing meditation, find a quiet place to sit or lie down, close your eyes, and focus on deep breathing. Visualize a white or golden light surrounding you, removing any negative energy, and filling you with positivity.

How to use spiritual cleansing for specific problems

Spiritual cleansing is used to address specific problems and challenges in life. Here are some ways to use spiritual cleansing for specific problems:

  • For emotional distress: Take a spiritual bath using herbs or essential oils that promote emotional balance and well-being, such as lavender or chamomile. Focus on letting go of negative emotions and visualizing positive, loving energy flowing into your body.
  • For physical ailments: Use smudging to cleanse your aura and physical space. Focus on the smoke removing any negative energy from your body and surrounding you with positive energy. You can also take a spiritual bath using Epsom salts and essential oils that promote physical healing, such as peppermint or eucalyptus.
  • For spiritual blockages: Perform a meditation to cleanse your spirit. Concentrate on your breathing and your emotions that may be blocking your spiritual growth and try to balance them.
  • For stress and anxiety: Use smudging or a spiritual bath to release stress and promote relaxation. Focus on letting go of stress and anxiety and visualize calm and peace flowing into your body.
  • For negative energy in space: Use smudging to cleanse a physical space, such as your home or office, of negative energy. Emphasis on the smoke removing any negative energy and filling the space with positive energy.

Tips for successful spiritual cleansing

Spiritual cleansing is a powerful practice that brings balance and positivity to the body, mind, and spirit. To achieve the best results from spiritual cleansing, it is important to follow some key tips and guidelines.

  • Set a clear intention: Before starting your spiritual cleansing, take a moment to set a clear intention for the practice. Think about what you hope to achieve and what you want to release. This will help you focus your mind and energy during the process.
  • Create a peaceful environment: Find a quiet, peaceful place where you are able to perform your spiritual cleansing without distractions. Such as in your home, in nature, or in a quiet room at a spiritual center.
  • Use appropriate tools: There are many tools that are used in spiritual cleansing, such as sage, Palo Santo, herbs, salts, essential oils, and candles. Choose the tools that resonate with you and that you feel comfortable using.
  • Focus on your breathing: During your spiritual cleansing, focus on your breathing and try to let go of any thoughts or distractions. This will help you stay present in the moment and allow you to fully connect with the practice.
  • Trust the process: Trust that the spiritual cleansing process will work for you, even if you don’t see immediate results. Be patient and trust that the changes you seek will come in your own time.
  • Follow your intuition: Your intuition is a powerful tool that guides you through the spiritual cleansing process. If you feel drawn to a particular tool or technique, follow your intuition and trust that it is the right choice for you.
  • Practice regularly: Regular spiritual cleansing brings greater balance and positivity to your life. Make this practice a regular part of your spiritual routine and see how it positively impacts your life.

In conclusion, following these tips will help you achieve greater success in your spiritual cleansing practice. Remember to be patient, trust the process, and follow your intuition. With time and practice, you will see the positive impact that spiritual cleansing will have on your life. Use spiritual cleansing as a tool to support and enhance your overall well-being.

title.rendered: Therapeutic effects of SOMA Breath

content.rendered:
SOMA breath is a form of therapeutic breathing that has its roots in ancient practices and has been developed over the years to address modern-day challenges. The history of SOMA breath can be traced back to traditional practices such as pranayama in yoga and the shamanic use of breathwork in indigenous cultures.

In recent times, SOMA breath has evolved into a contemporary practice, drawing from various traditional techniques, and incorporating new technologies and techniques. The SOMA breath technique was developed by a team of experts in the fields of physiology, psychology, and spirituality, and has been scientifically researched and tested for its therapeutic benefits that are based on the principles of Ayurvedic medicine.

Since its inception, SOMA breath has been adopted by individuals and healthcare professionals around the world as an effective form of therapy for physical and mental well-being. The practice of SOMA breath has grown in popularity, and it is now being offered in wellness centers, yoga studios, and clinics as a complementary or alternative therapy for various health conditions.

The SOMA breath technique is now being used to treat a range of physical and mental health conditions, including stress, fear, depression, and insomnia, among others. The practice of SOMA breath continues to evolve, and new techniques and approaches are being developed to further enhance its therapeutic effects.

The full form of SOMA breath is “Somatic and Oral Mechanisms of Action” breath. SOMA breath is a form of breathwork that incorporates specific breathing patterns and sounds to help individuals achieve a state of deep relaxation and meditation.

Somatic refers to the body, and the technique aims to bring balance and harmony to the body by releasing tension and promoting deep relief. Oral refers to the sounds that are used during the technique, and the “mechanisms of action” refer to the way in which the technique works to bring about a desired effect.

SOMA breath is also believed to have a number of other benefits for physical and mental health. Some practitioners claim that the technique helps to improve sleep, boost the immune system, and even relieve pain.

Following are some of the other benefits of using SOMA breath. 

  • Improves relaxation: SOMA breath is a powerful tool for achieving deep relaxation, which leads to reduced stress, anxiety, and tension in the body.
  • Enhances mental and emotional well-being: Practicing SOMA breath helps to balance the mind and emotions, promoting a sense of inner peace and calm.
  • Increases energy levels: The deep relaxation achieved through SOMA breath also helps to increase energy levels and improve overall vitality.
  • Enhances sleep quality: SOMA breath can be used as a sleep aid and improves the quality of sleep.
  • Alleviates pain: SOMA breath enables release of stiffness and promotes deep relaxation in the body, which helps to alleviate pain and discomfort.
  • Improves cardiovascular health: SOMA breath tends to lower blood pressure and improve the overall health of the cardiovascular system.
  • Enhances spiritual connection: SOMA breath enables individuals to connect to their spiritual selves and promote a sense of inner wisdom and guidance.
  • Improves respiratory function: SOMA breath helps in improving the function of the respiratory system and increases lung capacity.
  • Enhances immune function: SOMA breath leads to strengthening the immune system and improves overall health.
  • Enhances overall well-being: Deep relaxation, improved mental well-being, and improved physical health all contribute to an overall sense of well-being.

How to use and store SOMA breath

Using SOMA breath is a simple process, but it is important to learn the technique from a trained practitioner to ensure proper use and avoid any risks. The SOMA breath technique involves breathing in through the nose and out through the mouth, using a specific pattern of inhale, hold, and exhale. The breath is also accompanied by specific sounds, such as “SOO” on the inhale and “MAA” on the exhale. These sounds are believed to resonate with the body’s energy centres, or chakras, to help balance and harmonize the body and mind.

When using SOMA breath, it is important to set a comfortable and quiet environment and to wear comfortable clothes. It is also important to be in a comfortable position, such as seated or lying down. With time as you practise more and more you may feel more relaxed.

When it comes to storing SOMA breath, it is not something that needs to be stored. It is a technique that can be practiced at anytime, anywhere, and as often as needed. However, if you are working with a trained specialist, they may provide you with some recordings, videos or other materials that are used as a guide to practice SOMA breath.

How to use SOMA breath therapeutically

SOMA breath therapeutically aims at controlling the rate, depth, and duration of breathing, SOMA breath helps to regulate the autonomic nervous system and balance the parasympathetic and sympathetic nervous system. This results in a calming effect on the body and mind, reducing symptoms of stress, anxiety, and depression.

In addition, SOMA breath has been found to improve sleep quality by inducing a state of relaxation and reducing sleep disturbances. The practice of SOMA breath has also been shown to have a positive impact bodies resistance, boosting immunity, and helping the body fight against diseases.

SOMA breath can be practiced by individuals of all ages and does not require any special equipment or training. It can be performed anywhere, at any time, making it a convenient and accessible form of therapy for those seeking to improve their mental and physical health.

However, it should be noted that SOMA breath is not a substitute for medical treatment and individuals with medical conditions should consult with a healthcare professional before trying the technique. Additionally, it is important to learn from a trained practitioner to ensure proper technique and avoid any risks.

title.rendered: Impact of Status Quo Bias Affects Your Decisions

content.rendered:
Introduction to the Status Quo Bias

The status quo bias refers to the tendency for individuals to prefer maintaining the current state of affairs over making a change. This bias is seen in various decision-making situations, such as investment choices, political voting, and consumer purchasing habits.

One reason for the existence of the status quo bias is that humans have a natural inclination towards the familiar. When faced with a decision, you tend to favor options that you are already familiar with and have a certain level of comfort with, rather than taking a risk on something new. Additionally, the status quo bias also stems from a lack of information or understanding about potential options. When faced with a complex decision, you default to sticking with the current situation because you are uncertain about the consequences of change.

Another reason for the status quo bias is the cognitive ease that comes with sticking with what is already known. Making a decision, especially a complex one, requires effort and mental energy. The status quo bias is seen as a form of mental laziness, as it allows us to avoid expending mental effort on evaluating choices.

The status quo bias has significant consequences in various areas of life. In business, it leads to missed opportunities for growth and innovation. In politics, it leads to the entrenchment of inefficient policies and systems. In personal finance, it leads to wrong decision-making in investment and retirement planning.

However, it is important to note that the status quo bias is not necessarily a negative thing. In certain situations, sticking with what is available may be the best decision. The key is to be aware of the bias and to actively consider substitutes before making a decision.

The Role of the Status Quo Bias in Decision-making

Status quo bias has a considerable influence on decision-making, as it makes individuals overlook potential substitutes and make decisions based on the familiar rather than what may be the best option.

  • Business- In business, the status quo bias makes managers stick with established practices and play safe which hampers growth and innovation. For example, a company may continue to rely on a traditional marketing strategy despite evidence that a new approach may be more effective.
  • Personal finance- In personal finance, the status quo bias makes individuals stick with familiar investment options rather than seek out more adventurous investments. For instance, an individual may continue to invest in a familiar stock rather than explore other options that may have a higher potential return.
  • Retirement planning – Similarly, the status quo bias leads to missed opportunities for retirement planning, as individuals tend to stick with traditional savings options rather than exploring new ways to invest and grow their savings.
  • Consumer purchasing habits- The status quo bias is also seen in consumer purchasing habits. Consumers tend to stick with familiar brands and products, rather than considering options that are more effective or cost-efficient.

The Impact of the Status Quo Bias on Judgments and Decisions

One way in which the status quo bias affects judgments is by causing individuals to overestimate the value of the status quo. This leads to a failure to consider potential choices, as individuals may believe that the current state of affairs is the best option available. Additionally, due to status quo bias, individuals underestimate the potential benefits of change, causing them to overlook opportunities for improvement. In addition, the status quo bias also makes an individual lack confidence in decision-making. When individuals are not considering options, they may not have a complete understanding of the situation and may lack confidence in their decision.

Limitations of the Status Quo Bias

Status quo bias has a significant impact on decision-making, it also has a number of limitations that ultimately provides suboptimal outcomes.

  • Another limitation of the status quo bias is that it leads to a lack of innovation. By sticking with the familiar, individuals may be less likely to explore new ideas and approaches, which inhibits progress and development.
  • The status quo bias also leads to a lack of confidence in decisions
  • Additionally, the status quo bias leads to a failure to adapt to changing conditions. A company may continue to rely on an outdated business model, rather than adapting to changing market conditions.

Ways to Overcome the Status Quo Bias

  • One way to overcome the status quo bias is to gather information on alternatives and evaluate them objectively. This is done by comparing the potential benefits and drawbacks of each option, as well as the potential risks and rewards. By taking the time to consider alternatives, individuals make a more informed decision and avoid the trap of sticking with the familiar.
  • Another way to overcome the status quo bias is to seek out the advice of experts or consult with others. This provides individuals with new perspectives and insights, which helps to broaden their understanding of the situation and potentially identify new alternatives.
  • A third way to overcome the status quo bias is to set a specific decision-making process and stick to it. This help to ensure that all alternatives are considered and that the decision is based on objective criteria, rather than emotional biases.
  • Another way to overcome the status quo bias is to be aware of the psychological and emotional context that affects the bias. The status quo bias is intensified in situations where the decision-maker is anxious, or the social context is uncertain. By being aware of these contextual factors, individuals take steps to reduce their impact and make a more informed decision.
  • Additionally, regularly reviewing and updating decision-making processes and strategies help to overcome the status quo bias.

In conclusion, the impact of status quo bias has a substantial impact on your decision-making process. It leads you to make choices that are not in your best interest, simply because they align with what you currently have or what you are used to. It is important to be aware of this bias and actively try to overcome it by considering alternative options and critically evaluating the pros and cons of each one. By doing this, it ensures that your decisions are based on logical reasoning and not just a preference for what is familiar.

title.rendered: Self-Reflection

content.rendered:
What is self-reflection?

Self-reflection is the process of thinking about one’s own thoughts and experiences in order to understand them better and gain insight. It’s not uncommon to experience something unusual that often makes you feel uneasy or get upset. Probably you lost your temper or got involved in a fight that made you feel low. If you have been in this situation, then self-reflection can help you to find out the real reason for your reaction and help you find a direction. The best thing about self-reflection is that it instantaneously provides you with a resolution rather than simply pondering on and judging yourself for a long time. Self-reflection helps you cross over that bridge and move on and simultaneously let you know what influenced you and what made you react in a certain manner.

Upon self-reflection when you realize what made you feel bad,  you can then decide not to repeat that behaviour in the future. Always give yourself comfort and compassion and be forgiving to self and others. This way you can turn the negativity into positivity.

title.rendered: Why are Relationships so hard?

content.rendered:
Relationships are undeniably tough, and for most of us they present the most hard-earned lessons in life. But why are relationships so hard to deal with? How come most of us struggle to ever find someone we feel truly loved and accepted by? And why are we always struggling to live harmoniously with our significant others?

WHY are relationships so hard and even impossible for many of us to keep and maintain?

Why Are Relationships So Hard, Frustrating and Painful?

I will be the first one to admit that I haven’t been the perfect romantic partner (who has?). I have, nagged, rejected and isolated myself many times in the past to my own detriment and to my partners. The only difference is that I have stepped up and admitted my wrongdoing. I have adopted an iron-willed determination to resolve this type of destructive behavior and have actively sought to learn from my mistakes for my own self-growth and also for the health of my relationships.

I’m not perfect – neither are you, and neither is your partner – which is why I recommend reading through the list below with an open mind. It’s easy to point the finger of blame at your partner for creating all the problems, but it is much harder to be honest with yourself and accept responsibility as well.

Here are the top 4 reasons why relationships seem so hard in my experience:

1. Because we impose our desires, expectations and beliefs onto our partners.

When we are constantly forcing our partner to be anything other than what they authentically are we create an immense amount of tension in our relationships. Essentially we are saying to them, “You are not good enough as you are and you better change or I won’t love you/treat you nicely.” Mostly we are unaware of our tendency to force our stories down our partner’s throats, and so we wind up in endless cycles of drama.

Examples of desires, expectations and beliefs include for instance “You should do this or else …” “You should behave like this because …” “You shouldn’t do that …” “You have to like/dislike this …”

What to do: Try to explore what ways you force your desires, expectations and beliefs onto your partner (or how they do it to you). You will be able to tell by the feeling of tension that arises in your body. This tension is a product of resistance, not acceptance.

2. Because of our inability to communicate openly and honestly (without repercussion).

Once upon a time I used to think that I was great at communicating. That was until I entered a serious long-term relationship. Since then I’ve discovered my tendency to believe that everyone can read my mind. I assume that they can understand me, and I assume that everyone else that I’m close with can miraculously read my thoughts. The reality is that they can’t.

The number #1 mistake most of us make in our relationships is our inability to communicate openly. Because of our fear and insecurity, most of us clamp up and interact in vague, ambiguous way to avoid clashes. And even if we DO courageously venture to tell the truth to our partners, we are often met with anger, emotional blackmail, and even plain hostility.

What to do: Can you communicate clearly and honestly about what you do and don’t like in your relationship? Do you struggle to be assertive, or does your partner? If so, this is a sign that there isn’t enough open communication. You need to jointly work together to create a “safe place” in which both parties strive to maintain open minds and compassionate hearts.

3. Because we project our childhood traumas onto our partners.

We don’t do this consciously of course, but projecting our childhood core traumas onto our partners is a big reason why our relationships can seem so hard. Our core wounds are formed in childhood, and often what we experienced in early life sets a tone for what we experience in later life. For instance, if I grew up with an emotionally cold and distant mother, it is likely that in later life I would seek a partner that fills that void, e.g. who is overly possessive, controlling and smothering with affection. Or else I might attract the same type of woman (cold and distant) who I unconsciously seek to “right wrongs” with and win the affection of in an attempt to soother my core wound of feeling “unlovable.”

What to do: Treating or relying on your partner as you would a parent is a big red flag – and feeling like a parent is an even bigger one. Does this ring true to your own relationship? Do you feel like a father or mother who constantly needs to scold, punish or nurture your partner? Do you feel like a child that is subservient to your partner’s position of “higher authority”? If so, you need to clearly identify and explore the core wound that is driving your behavior. It takes two to tango.

4. Because of our lack of authentic self-love.

Our love in relationships feels so conditional because the truth is that we don’t really know how to love unconditionally. Why? Because we haven’t learned how to love ourselves. Jesus said about love: “Love your neighbor as yourself.” How can you love your neighbor if you don’t know how to first love yourself? How can you give to another what you don’t possess in the first place?

Self-love is a vital part of any relationship as it builds a foundation of authentic, healthy and pure love. Without self-love, our relationships are fueled by neediness, obsession, fear, jealousy and pain. Without self-love we will always be motivated by some furtive and even sinister unfulfilled need. But with self-love, we are no longer motivated by anything other than the desire to give because we already have everything we need – from ourselves.

What to do:  A healthy (and EASIER) relationship depends on how much self-love you have. Self-love does not mean being narcissistic, nor does it mean prancing about with rose-tinted glasses on, but it refers to the development of a profound inner acceptance and understanding of yourself.

Time to Reflect

What keywords or concept have stood out to you in this article? Pay attention to how you feel. Defensive? Angry? Sad? Surprised? Weary? And what does this reveal?

Why are relationships so hard? In my experience, it all boils down to how aware vs. unaware we are of our own authentic needs, desires, strengths, flaws and tendencies.

And this applies to any and all relationships whether intimate or otherwise. As human beings we bring our inner struggles into every relationship.

title.rendered: Energy Imbalances Cause Disease and Suffering

content.rendered:
Quantum physics has acknowledged that we are all made up of energy, as is everything around us. It is the most basic building block of life, but like the air we breathe most people can’t see it. Energy flows through everything and creates everything. Even our thoughts and emotions are energy. It is just a difference in the vibrational frequency of energy that gives us the illusion of substance and separation, rather like water moving from solid ice at slower vibration, to fluids and then to steam at higher vibrations.

Our personal energies are delicately balanced and we can become sick or feel “not quite right” when our energy flows are disturbed or blocked. Energy imbalances can result from both internal and external factors.

Internal factors impacting our energy system include:

  • trauma
  • phobias
  • anxiety & stress
  • childhood programming
  • limiting beliefs
  • neurological, biochemical and structural imbalances
  • existential fears and limiting spiritual beliefs
  • remaining in situations that are not fulfilling or in harmony with our needs

External factors impacting our energy systems include:

  • environmental stresses & toxins
  • geopathic phenomena
  • astrological phenomena
  • nutrition
  • exercise
  • posture

During our early life we start collecting information that determines our programming. Genetic, social and cultural aspects will contribute to this programming. Over the years these pictures and programs we collect will govern the way we use our energy. We hold the information in our subtle energy systems and it determines how the energy moves through our chakras. The pictures or programs will remain there until such time as we start to realize that we create our experiences with the beliefs we hold – good and bad.

It’s sometimes acknowledged by my clients that they either did not, or currently do not, get along with one of their parents. It’s often rationalized as a “personality clash”. This is often reflected in other relationships with the same sex as the parent in question. This type of pattern can sometimes be seen in their own parents, grandparents and so on. The problem is, we generally do not know enough of our family history to be able to trace it back more than one or two generations. Many people like to blame their last failed relationship on many causes. Though some relationship problems can be traced back along the ancestral line, sometimes just one or two generations, and sometimes many more. The actual cause of the inherited pattern or imbalance could have been created in any number of ways. But, clear that energetic imbalance back in time, and life has a way of moving forward in a much more positive way.

Hereditary imbalances are seen on a regular basis. How or why is usually unknown, until we dig down to the cause in a healing session. So when you say to me, “I just don’t understand where this is coming from, it seems like something outside of myself”, it is understandable. And what’s more, we can clear genetic hereditary patterns of the ancestors and the descendants. Oftentimes with astounding results.

The energy systems of the body (aura, chakras, nadis and meridians) are connected energetically to our physical organs, glands and bodily systems. When the energy supplied to these bodily systems is disrupted, the body organs and systems are less able to defend against disease and injury.

Humans are a latticework of energies:
